svg.title: Proposed Syn distributed ledger architecture
svg.desc: People and agents sign knowledge records. Scoped peer replication exchanges authorised records. Community consensus finalises permissions, ontology adoption and batch admission. A deterministic reducer builds verifiable local views. Existing PostgreSQL, libp2p and receipt services are foundations; the ledger components shown are proposed.
svg.text: A shared history, with room to disagree
Syn ledger proposal · 23 October 2026 · architecture illustration
People, communities, applications and agents
Create signed records under explicit capabilities. Private drafts stay local.
Human identity, application signing keys and libp2p peer identity remain distinct.
Signed knowledge graph
Observations · claims · evidence · amendments
Author chains and causal parent digests
Scoped replication through libp2p
Peer receipt is provisional; it is not shared finality.
Community control log
Permissions · keys · ontology · batch admission
One authoritative outcome within each domain
Maintained BFT engine and Syn reducer
CometBFT reference; Hiero/Hashgraph comparison.
Available signed records
Finalised outcomes
Deterministic admission, checkpoints and local projection
Verify signatures, authority, dependencies and proofs; retain rejected outcomes.
Agreement establishes the accepted record and policy, not the truth of a claim.
PostgreSQL query views and evidence storage
Existing Syn objects and v1 receipts remain compatible; new ledger tables are planned.
Dashed boxes: proposed ledger responsibilities. Solid storage box: an existing foundation to extend.
No global truth score · no automatic token economy · no automatic execution of messages
